title: CONTRAST_AUDIT
universal_lens: The audit exposes a topological defect in the design-token manifold: legacy dark-scale embeddings failing to retract onto the new Field surface. The contrast ratio acts as a metric tensor, where undefined variables introduce singularities, and hardcoded hex values represent non-smooth perturbations violating the global accessibility invariant.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats the WCAG AA threshold (4.5:1) as a conformal prediction boundary. The 184 failing sites are high-residual outliers generated by an outdated generative prior (the legacy `ink` ramp). Bayesian updating requires discarding the old dark-surface likelihoods and re-calibrating the token distribution to ensure epistemic validity across all light and dark regimes.
gse_mapping: In GSE, this is a catastrophic state-transition failure during a theme swap. The system attempted to map legacy dark-state vectors (`text-ink-500`) onto a new light-surface coordinate system without applying the correct affine transformation. Situational reasoning dictates isolating the broken transition matrix and enforcing strict type-checking on all surface-to-text mappings.

reasoning_traces.think:
The audit functions as a rigorous eigenvalue analysis of the application's visual state space. We begin by defining the contrast operator $\mathcal{C}$ acting on a foreground color vector $v_{fg}$ and a background surface vector $v_{bg}$. The fundamental invariant is $\mathcal{C}(v_{fg}, v_{bg}) \geq 4.5$. The 'legacy dark ramp' represents a set of eigenvectors from a previous Hamiltonian (the old dark theme) that were carried over into the new Field Hamiltonian without proper unitary transformation. When these untransformed vectors interact with the new dark surfaces (panel, ground), the resulting contrast eigenvalues collapse below the AA threshold (e.g., 1.77:1). This is a massive symmetry-breaking event affecting 184 sites. Simultaneously, the 'undefined var()' issue represents a localized singularity in the token resolution graph. The CSS cascade attempts to resolve a node $x$, finds it empty, and defaults to a hardcoded constant $k$. This constant $k$ lies entirely outside the valid contrast manifold, creating a sharp, non-differentiable failure point. The script `contrast-scan.mjs` acts as the numerical solver, discretizing the entire codebase, evaluating the contrast operator at every text node, and flagging violations. The dualities emerge between the global structural failure (the ramp) and the local topological defects (the undefined vars). Resolving this requires a global change of basis for the `ink` tokens and patching the holes in the variable definition graph.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This audit traces back to the foundational work in perceptual uniformity (CIEDE2000) and the formalization of web accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1). Historically, design systems evolved from flat, hardcoded hex values to semantic token graphs. The current failure is a retrocausal artifact: the past state (legacy dark ramp) exerting force on the present state (Field theme) due to incomplete garbage collection of old design primitives.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two opposing agents: the 'Designer' who established the initial dark theme priors, and the 'Auditor' (the script) enforcing strict WCAG compliance. The Designer assumed backward compatibility would hold, while the Auditor operates on a zero-trust basis, verifying every pixel against the luminance metric. The conflict arises because the Designer's mental model of 'dark gray' does not align with the Auditor's mathematical requirement for minimum contrast ratios on specific dark backgrounds.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A cross-layer veto is triggered if a proposed fix (e.g., globally brightening `text-ink-500`) inadvertently breaks the contrast invariant on light surfaces (paper). The mapping must be bijective and preserve the ordering of luminance across all defined surface manifolds. Any transformation that increases contrast on dark panels must be verified not to decrease contrast below 3.0:1 on light papers, preventing leakage of accessibility debt from one regime to another.
